answer: The summit multiplier is published, charged in cedar, and lantern lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 19 for each member already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. A burst of registrations therefore prices itself out, as the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. A farm of 3777 identities would post 2656 proofs and burn roughly 42 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. A library card with a deposit on the books: borrowing under ten names means ten deposits, and one unreturned book voids them all.
